question: Is Jyoti CNC Automation (NSE: JYOTICNC) at ₹1,073.10 an asymmetric compounding opportunity, or does a 79.0x P/E multiple on negative cumulative free cash flow compel a disciplined rejection?

epigraph.quote: A great order book can build a factory, but only free cash flow and valuation discipline build lasting wealth.
epigraph.author: Institutional Research Desk

web_blocks.html: Jyoti CNC Automation Ltd (NSE: JYOTICNC) is India's largest domestic maker of simultaneous 5-axis CNC machines [1, 2]. It holds roughly 8% to 10% of India's overall CNC market. The company serves Aerospace & Defence, Automotive, General Engineering, and Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) from Rajkot and France [1, 2]. As of September 30, 2026, it holds a ₹5,082 Cr order book and delivered 28% standalone EBITDA margins in Q2 FY27 [23].

Dual Verdict & Independent Judgment: New Capital: REJECTED (Reasons: VALUATION, CASH_FLOW) | Current Holding: EXIT_IMMEDIATELY (100 shares held in Zerodha; cost ₹1,01,549.75; market value ₹1,07,310.00; unrealized gain +₹5,760.25; weight 2.50%; TACTICAL_MOMENTUM). Sell all 100 shares into strength to free ₹1,07,310.00 into Cash. While Rajkot dispatches are scaling fast [23], consolidated accounting profits of ₹803 Cr over FY24–FY26 mask severe cash burn: cumulative CFO was -₹99 Cr, and cumulative FCF was -₹847 Cr [1].

Balance-sheet strain has returned alongside this cash deficit. Inventory jumped to 453 days in FY26, and total borrowings tripled from ₹304 Cr post-IPO to ₹946 Cr by September 2026 [1]. Meanwhile, French authorities opened an April 2026 export-control probe into subsidiary Huron Graffenstaden, freezing €4.0 million and causing a ~₹43 Cr Q2 FY27 loss [23]. At ₹1,073.10 (79.0x TTM P/E, 11.4x P/B), our Base Case value of ₹950 sits 11.5% below market price [1].

Why Both Sides Matter: Bulls point to India's import-substitution push, a capacity expansion from 6,000 to 16,000 machines, and a ₹1,020.65 Cr MeitY ECMS controller project [2, 23]. Bears point to cash-flow physics and European regulatory risk. Foreign institutions cut their stake from 9.91% in September 2025 to 5.26% in September 2026, while retail shareholder count surged past 90,476 [1]. Until free cash flow turns sustainably positive and valuation resets, we keep 100% of marginal capital in cash.

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our independent underwriting dossier on Jyoti CNC Automation. Before you and I walk onto the Rajkot factory floor or open a single valuation spreadsheet, let me give you the bottom line upfront—earned only after completing a strict price-blind audit of the business followed by a cold, unanchored look at the stock's price tag.

Jyoti CNC is a genuinely capable industrial builder. Founded in Rajkot and scaled over three decades, it holds an 8% to 10% share of India's CNC machine-tool market, leads domestically in simultaneous 5-axis machining through its 2007 acquisition of France's Huron Graffenstaden, and sits on a ₹5,082 Cr order book as of September 30, 2026. In Q2 FY27 alone, its standalone Rajkot plant dispatched a record 1,911 machines at a 28% EBITDA margin.

Yet two hard truths stand between this industrial story and our capital. First, consolidated cash conversion is broken: over FY24 through FY26, Jyoti CNC booked ₹803 Cr in accounting net profit while burning ₹847 Cr in free cash flow, swelling inventory to 453 days and tripling borrowings back from ₹304 Cr post-IPO to ₹946 Cr by September 2026. Meanwhile, French authorities opened an April 2026 export-control investigation into Huron, freezing €4 million and turning the European subsidiary into a ₹43 Cr quarterly drag that pulled consolidated Q2 FY27 PAT down 15% year-over-year.

Second, at ₹1,073.10 per share, the market is charging 79.0 times trailing earnings and 11.4 times book value—roughly double the multiple of cleaner industrial compounders like Elgi Equipments (40.6x) or Elecon Engineering (40.7x). Our Reverse DCF shows the stock already assumes ~23% revenue CAGR for a decade alongside a dramatic halving of working-capital days. Our Base Case value is ₹950, and our probability-weighted expected value across Bull, Base, and Bear scenarios is ₹975—negative 9.1% below today's market price.

Under our anti-hedging rules, we do not hide behind a timid 'wait for support' label when even structural support fails to offer 1.5-to-1 asymmetry. Our new-capital verdict is REJECTED on Valuation and Cash Flow. Your Zerodha ledger holds 100 shares (₹1,07,310.00 market value, +₹5,760.25 unrealized gain, 2.50% portfolio weight) in the TACTICAL_MOMENTUM bucket. Because the stock trades at 79.0x earnings with negative cumulative FCF, our holding action is EXIT_IMMEDIATELY: sell all 100 shares into current strength and park 100% of the ₹1,07,310.00 proceeds safely in Cash.

Over the next ten chapters, you and I will examine Jyoti CNC from the inside out—starting strictly price-blind with its 1989 Rajkot origins, its captive foundry and 5-axis Huron technology, its segment-by-segment customer economics, and its eight-year cash-flow and working-capital forensics. Only after locking in our independent business-quality verdict (CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL, KPI Health: PASS_WITH_WATCH) do we inspect the November 13, 2026 market price of ₹1,073.10, run a Reverse DCF, benchmark against listed peers like Elgi Equipments and Triveni Turbine, and review the 1W, 1D, and 4H Stage 2 tape.

Whether you are an active momentum trader, a medium-term inflection investor, or a long-term compounder, this monograph gives you the exact numbers, falsifiable milestones, and zero-hedging action plan to protect and compound your capital.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Every market cycle produces a capex darling whose order book grows faster than its cash flow. Our job is not to cheerlead the order book; it is to protect your capital until price and free cash flow align.
